analysis.title: US Weekly Kickstart: Q3 2026 earnings season preview
key_insights: Q3 2026 earnings season starts the week of October 12 with 7% of S&P 500 market cap reporting. About 70% will have reported by the end of October. Most hyperscalers report the last week of October and Nvidia is expected the third week of November.

Consensus expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y in Q3, the highest heading into any reporting season since 2021. This compares with 33% realized in Q2, excluding the 'other income' from appreciating equity stakes. GS expects another quarter of above-consensus results.
Options imply an average 5.4% move for the average S&P 500 stock on the day after reporting. The average implied move over the past 4 quarters was 5.5% and the average realized move was 5.1%.

Info Tech and Energy contribute nearly 80% of expected Q3 EPS growth. The median stock in each is expected to grow EPS by more than 30%. Consumer sectors show no aggregate EPS growth in bottom-up estimates.

AI infrastructure stocks are expected to drive more than half of S&P 500 Q3 EPS growth. The top 10 contributors account for over two-thirds, and Micron and Nvidia together account for more than 1/3 of index growth.
Micron reported on September 30 with y/y earnings growth of 1,003%, beat consensus EPS estimates and gave strong forward guidance. GS calls it a strong start to the season.
Breadth is at its narrowest since the Dot Com Bubble. The index is 2% from its all-time high while the median stock is 17% below its own. Earnings and returns are both supported mainly by Info Tech.
For the median S&P 500 stock, consensus EPS growth slows from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3. Growth decelerates in every sector except Info Tech and Comm Services.

Median-stock sales growth is expected to slow from 7% in Q2 to 6% in Q3. GS economists estimate nominal GDP grew 6% y/y in Q3, similar to Q2. The weaker dollar added about 2 pp to S&P 500 revenue growth in Q1 and 1 pp in Q2, and likely under 1 pp in Q3.

Input cost pressures likely limit sequential margin expansion. Consensus has the median stock's net margin at 14.7% in Q3 versus 15.1% in Q2. Analysts cut Q3 median margin estimates by 11 bp since the start of the quarter, in every sector except Info Tech.

Consensus has hyperscaler capex growing 116% y/y in Q3 versus 87% in Q2. GS expects 2027 hyperscaler capex growth above 50%, above the roughly $1.1 trillion consensus, but expects both capex growth and upside surprises to diminish. GS does not expect clarity on capex beyond 2027 this season.
AI monetization is a key theme. Hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated to 48% in Q2 alongside large backlogs, and GS equity analysts expect 55% in Q3.
About 50% of S&P 500 firms discussed AI productivity or efficiency on last quarter's calls, but only 2% quantified the earnings impact. GS expects both shares to rise gradually.
Mega-cap tech booked roughly $150 billion of accounting profit last quarter from appreciating equity stakes, equal to 12% of S&P 500 EPS. GS does not expect a meaningful repeat in Q3.

Tariff refunds were $77 billion in Q2 and $69 billion in Q3, about 6% of US corporate pre-tax profits each quarter. An Atlanta Fed survey shows most firms plan to keep the refunds in cash or invest in R&D or capital projects.
GS top-down S&P 500 forecasts: year-end 2026 target 8000 (about 4% above the current 7666) and 12-month target 8700. GS EPS is $375 for 2026 and $415 for 2027, with the S&P 500 on 19x NTM EPS.

sector_views.rationale: Consensus Q3 EPS growth of 64% on 42% sales growth and a 427 bp margin change. Estimates are the only sector with Q3 margin revisions upward.
Consensus Q3 EPS growth of 109% with a 640 bp margin change. Energy and Info Tech together drive nearly 80% of aggregate EPS growth.
Bottom-up consensus shows 0% and (0)% aggregate Q3 EPS growth, with margin changes of (18) bp and (34) bp.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth: consensus est +27% y/y (not yet reported). Q2 realized +33% y/y excluding other income from equity stakes.
Median S&P 500 stock Q3 EPS growth: consensus est +9% y/y versus +14% realized in Q2. Median sales growth consensus est 6% versus 7% in Q2.
Micron (MU) reported Q3 results September 30: y/y earnings growth of 1,003%, beat consensus EPS estimates, strong forward guidance.
Expected report dates: GOOGL October 27, BA October 27, META October 29, AMZN October 30, XOM October 30, CVX October 30, MPC November 3, NVDA November 19, AVGO December 11.
Contribution to consensus Q3 y/y S&P 500 EPS growth (est): MU 19%, NVDA 15%, META 7%, GOOGL 6%, AVGO 5%, XOM 4%, AMZN 4%, BA 3%, CVX 3%, MPC 3%. Top 10 total 68%.

Consensus Q3 sector EPS growth (est): Energy 109%, Info Tech 64%, Comm Services 38%, Materials 36%, Industrials 16%, Real Estate 15%, Utilities 6%, Health Care 5%, Financials 1%, Consumer Discretionary 0%, Consumer Staples (0)%.
Hyperscaler Q3 capex consensus est +116% y/y. Cloud revenue growth for AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT and ORCL: GS est 55% in Q3 versus 48% reported in Q2.
GS 2026 S&P 500 EPS $375 versus bottom-up consensus $365 and top-down strategist consensus $355.

risk_factors: Input cost pressures may limit sequential margin expansion, with Q3 median margin estimates cut in every sector except Info Tech.
The dollar tailwind to S&P 500 revenue growth shrinks to under 1 pp in Q3 from 1 pp in Q2.
Concentration risk: top 10 contributors drive over two-thirds of Q3 EPS growth, and MU plus NVDA more than 1/3.
Uncertainty about 2028 AI capex spending is the focus of investor conversations, and companies are not expected to clarify it this season.
GS expects capex growth and upside surprises to diminish relative to recent quarters.
Median stock EPS growth slows in every sector except Info Tech and Comm Services.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows the share of S&P 500 market cap reporting by week: 7% the week of Oct 12, 14% Oct 19, 44% Oct 26, 13% Nov 2, 2% Nov 9, 11% Nov 16.
Exhibit 14 shows AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT and ORCL cloud revenue growth rising from 24% in Q1 2024 to 48% in Q2 2026, with GS estimates of 55% for Q3 and 56% for Q4.
Exhibit 17 shows monthly 2026 customs-duty refunds peaking at $51 billion in June.
Exhibit 18 shows 75% of firms receiving or seeking tariff refunds plan to keep them in cash and 53% to invest in R&D or capital projects.
vol_and_positioning: Options imply a 5.4% average next-day move for S&P 500 stocks reporting this quarter, versus 5.5% average implied over the past 4 quarters and 5.1% realized.
GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator reads (0.7) as of October 2, 2026. The report labels above 1.0 as stretched positioning and below (1.0) as light positioning.
S&P 500 3-month realized average stock correlation is 0.06 per the exhibit.
Market breadth (index distance from 52-week high minus median stock's) is at its narrowest since the Dot Com Bubble. Top 10 companies are 40% of S&P 500 market cap and 37% of earnings.

tension_points.theme: Q3 earnings beat versus narrowing growth
tension_points.bull_case: Consensus 27% EPS growth is the highest since 2021 and GS expects most companies to surpass it. Recent growth data are strong and revision breadth stays positive.
tension_points.bear_case: Median stock EPS growth slows from 14% to 9%, input costs cap margin expansion, the dollar tailwind fades, and growth and returns are concentrated in Info Tech with breadth at its lowest since the Dot Com Bubble.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex is expected up 116% y/y in Q3 and GS sees cloud growth accelerating to 55% on large backlogs, with 2027 capex growth above 50%.
tension_points.bear_case: Investor uncertainty centers on 2028 spending and GS expects capex growth and upside surprises to diminish. Only 2% of companies quantify AI earnings gains.
